temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small, 5–6 oz (170 g) 400°F / 205°C · 32 min 425°F / 220°C · 43 min Medium, 8–10 oz (250 g) 400°F / 205°C · 40 min 425°F / 220°C · 53 min Large, 12 oz (350 g) and over 400°F / 205°C · 50 min 425°F / 220°C · 67 min Crisp skin, hard middle A potato is dense, and heat moves slowly through it. In an air fryer the skin crisps and darkens long before the centre is cooked, so a potato can look finished while the middle is still waxy and firm. A fork is a poor test because it slides into a partly cooked potato almost as easily as a done one. The reliable test is temperature: starch only turns fluffy when the centre reaches about 205°F. The table times assume potatoes of similar size cooked together. If you mix sizes, the small ones will be done first; take them out and give the large ones the extra minutes. Worked example Two medium russets, about 9 oz each, scrubbed, dried, rubbed with oil and coarse salt, and pricked a few times. Cook at 400°F for 40 minutes, turning them at 20 minutes. Small potatoes need about 32 minutes and large ones about 50. The same potatoes take 425°F for around 53 minutes in a conventional oven, so the air fryer saves a good quarter of an hour. How to tell it is done Push a thermometer into the centre: 205–210°F (96°C) means the starch has cooked through and the inside will be fluffy. Without a thermometer, squeeze the potato gently in a towel; it should give easily all the way through. The skin should be dry, crisp and slightly blistered. Cut it open straight away to let the steam out, or the inside turns gummy. Before it goes in Choose floury potatoes such as russets or Maris Pipers; waxy potatoes stay dense. Scrub and dry them completely, then rub with a little oil and plenty of coarse salt, which draws moisture from the skin. Prick each potato a few times with a fork. Do not wrap them in foil: foil traps steam and gives soft skin. About 40 minutes at 400°F for a medium 8–10 oz potato, turned at 20 minutes. Small potatoes take around 32 minutes, large ones around 50. What internal temperature is a baked potato done at? 205–210°F (96°C) in the centre. Below that the middle stays waxy, however crisp the skin looks. Should I wrap potatoes in foil in the air fryer? No. Foil traps steam and leaves the skin soft. Oil and coarse salt on bare skin gives the crisp jacket the air fryer is good at. Do I need to prick potatoes before air frying? Yes, a few times with a fork. It lets steam escape and stops the occasional potato from splitting. What is the oven equivalent for a baked potato? 425°F for around 53 minutes in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 44 minutes in a fan oven.
